title: Full Strategy Walkthrough
hook: The whole model in one walk: the story, three breaks, two corrections, one zone, one retest, and your decision.

launchpad.outcome: Walk the complete strategy from the HTF story to the final entry or no-trade decision, and know where to keep practising.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Can you call every step of the sequence before the chart shows it?

takeaways: Higher-timeframe ICC sets the direction. The 15M gives BOS #1. The 5M builds the rest.
Correction #1 never creates the zone. Correction #2 does, and BOS #3 activates it.
The entry waits for the retest. No retest, no trade.
An invalidated zone or an incomplete sequence is a no-trade decision.

slides.headline: The whole model, start to finish.
slides.line: One last walk: the story, three breaks, two corrections, one zone, one retest. Then you decide.

slides.headline: Every trade starts with the story.
slides.line: Tap each card. This is the HTF (higher timeframe) context for this chart.

cards.label: 4H context
cards.sub: Bearish. Price is in the upper half of the 4H range and correcting.

cards.label: 1H structure
cards.sub: Bearish 1H structure. Price is reacting from a 1H lower high.

cards.label: HTF ICC
cards.sub: HTF ICC: bearish Indication, Correction in progress.

check.prompt: What are you looking for on the lower timeframes?

options.label: A bearish sequence and a supply zone
options.why: Right. Higher-timeframe ICC supplies the direction. Here it’s bearish, so you look for a bearish sequence and a supply zone.

options.label: A bullish sequence and a demand zone
options.feedback: Read the cards again. The 4H, the 1H and the HTF ICC are all bearish.

slides.headline: Break on the 15M. Correct on the 5M.
slides.line: Press the button to print the 15M break, then switch to the 5M.

steps.caption: BOS #1 (break of structure). A 15M candle closes below the 15M level.
Correction #1. Price pulls back up on the 5M, toward the original 15M break.

check.prompt: Can Correction #1 create the execution zone?

options.label: Yes. Its last bullish candle is the supply zone
options.feedback: Not this one. Correction #1 never creates the execution zone. You still need BOS #2 and then Correction #2.

options.label: No. The zone comes from Correction #2
options.why: Right. Correction #1 never creates the execution zone. Correction #2 does, after BOS #2.

slides.headline: BOS #2 printed. Now find the second pullback.
slides.why: That’s inside Correction #2, the pullback after BOS #2. This is the correction that creates the zone.

after.caption: Correction #2. Now find the one candle in it that forms the zone.

slides.headline: One candle. Not the whole correction.
slides.line: For supply, the zone comes from the last bullish candle of Correction #2.
slides.ask: Tap the last bullish candle of Correction #2.
slides.why: That’s the zone-forming candle. It creates a potential supply zone.

after.caption: A potential supply zone, using the candle’s full high-to-low range. It isn’t active until BOS #3.

slides.headline: Activate the zone, then wait.
slides.line: Sellers need a 5M close below the low Correction #2 pulled back from.
slides.ask: Tap BOS #3: the first 5M candle that closes below that low.
slides.why: That’s BOS #3. The supply zone is now active. You don’t chase. You wait for price to come back.

after.caption: Price comes back up to the zone: the retest. The working model’s limit sits at the zone’s low, its near edge.

slides.headline: Full sequence. Now what happens?
slides.line: Bullish chart. BOS #3 has activated the demand zone. Press the button.

steps.caption: Price keeps rising and never returns to the zone.

options.label: Entry. The sequence was complete
options.feedback: The sequence completed, but the entry waits for the retest. Price never came back, so there’s no trade.

options.label: No trade. It’s a missed trade, so don’t chase
options.why: Right. No retest means no trade. A missed trade isn’t a trade, and you don’t chase price.

slides.headline: Same sequence. A different ending.
slides.line: Bullish chart. BOS #3 has activated the demand zone. Press the button.

steps.caption: A 5M candle closes below the zone’s low. The setup is invalid.
Price drifts back into the old zone.

check.prompt: Price is back in the old zone. Entry or no trade?

options.label: Entry. That’s the retest
options.feedback: A retest only counts while the zone is valid. After a 5M close below its low, you don’t treat it as an entry.

options.label: No trade. The zone was invalidated
options.why: Right. A 5M candle closed beyond the zone’s far edge, so the setup is invalid. Price coming back doesn’t make it an entry.

slides.headline: Now practise it until it’s automatic.
slides.line: Two practice labs in Strategy 2 let you rehearse everything from this module. Tap each one.

cards.label: The Zone Builder
cards.sub: Pick Correction #2, the zone candle and the boundaries, then judge if the zone is still valid.

cards.label: The Execution Lab
cards.sub: Read the HTF story, mark each step candle by candle, then choose entry or no trade.

slides.quote: Three breaks. Two corrections. One zone. One retest. Every time.
slides.line: Head to the Zone Builder and the Execution Lab next. Practise until you can call every step before it prints.

slides.prompt: Walk through the full strategy in your own words, from the 4H to the entry or no-trade decision.
slides.modelAnswer: I start with the 4H context, the 1H structure and location, and the HTF ICC to set the direction. Then I wait for BOS #1, a 15M candle close in that direction. On the 5M, Correction #1 pulls back and BOS #2 continues the move. Correction #2 follows, and its last opposite-colour candle forms the zone. BOS #3 activates the zone, and I wait for price to return to it. If price never returns, the zone is invalidated, or the sequence never completes, it’s no trade.
